2609.18642.title: STRETCH the Boundaries: A Unified Self-Taught Framework for Progressive LLM Evolution
2609.18642.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) often suffer from capability stagnation in self-improvement training because fixed difficulty levels fail to adapt to their evolving proficiency. To address this issue, we propose STRETCH (Self-Taught Reasoning Evolution via Targeted CHallenge), a unified framework inspired by cognitive scaffolding theory. STRETCH introduces a dynamic Stretch Zone mechanism that continuously aligns question difficulty with the model's solving capability. Within a single parameter space, the model alternates between a Scaffolder that generates adaptive, boundary-pushing challenges and a Learner that that optimizes its solving trajectories through reinforcement learning. This dual-loop co-evolution effectively stabilizes training, mitigates reward hacking and promote progressive reasoning growth. Experiments on both negotiation and operation research benchmarks demonstrate that STRETCH consistently outperforms strong prompting and domain-specific baselines. Further scaffolder configuration analysis shows that dynamic difficulty alignment is critical for sustained capability improvement and synchronized reasoning evolution.
2609.18642.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在自我改進訓練中常常面臨能力停滯的問題，因為固定的難度水平無法適應它們不斷增長的熟練度。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了STRETCH（通過針對性挑戰進行自我教學推理演變），這是一個受到認知支架理論啟發的統一框架。STRETCH引入了一個動態的伸展區域機制，持續將問題的難度與模型的解題能力對齊。在單一的參數空間內，模型在生成適應性、突破邊界挑戰的支架者和通過強化學習優化解題軌跡的學習者之間交替進行。這種雙循環的共同演化有效地穩定了訓練，減輕了獎勵駭客行為，並促進了漸進的推理增長。在談判和運營研究基準上的實驗表明，STRETCH始終優於強提示和特定領域的基準。此外，進一步的支架者配置分析顯示，動態難度對齊對於持續的能力提升和同步的推理演變至關重要。
